dimension: thesis_latex/body_appendix_short.tex (Appendix C protocols and exhaustiveness ladder, F dataset provenance, G ranking-recovery statistics, H supplementary statistics)
summary: Read all 1,413 lines. 54 sites depend on the single-instance convention; Appendices A, B, D (Orai1 receptor), E (pharmacology) and the Orai1 panel section C.7 (:359-482) carry no crystal-referenced number and are untouched. Derivable from the probe CSV (baselines reproduced exactly before substitution): the top-k Wilson table for 5 of 7 variants, the AutoDock and DiffDock-smina rows of the optimisation table, two rows of the cross-tool table, the accurate-but-invalid table, the exh128 rows of the ladder table, the depth-gain decomposition (+65/-2/+1/+64, +45/0/+2/+47, +27/-2/+1/+26), the validity-cost paragraph (at most five, 0.66-1.65 pp, raw DiffDock 65 and 18.8-21.5 pp), the H.9 Newcombe intervals (+5.6 [-1.7, +12.8] at rank-1; 129 discordant, MDD 10.5 pp, power 0.32, ~1,060 complexes needed; 90% interval -0.5 to +11.7 so rank-1 is no longer equivalent within 10 points, only within 12), the in-place rows of the threshold-resolved table and the cohort sizes of the placement/form table (190->249, 882->1147, 2200->2832 for AutoDock). Six clusters must be recomputed because the probe covers six arms and only in-place RMSD: (1) every Kabsch/form quantity (triple gate, three-part ladder endpoint, Kabsch rows, form medians, winner's curse, guided-EquiBind form block) needs a best-fit RMSD to the nearest copy the probe does not compute; (2) the other ladder rungs, Vinardo, DiffDock-gnina, EquiBind raw/smina and guided arms need the probe run with --arms (all 27 keys exist in the canonical table); (3) every contact/PLIF quantity (:543, :549, :551, :1405-1413, Fig r9) needs a per-copy native fingerprint because 139/143 alternate copies sit on another chain, which is the largest item; (4) the metal-adjacent stratum (:165) has no harness stage and its own definition is crystal-referenced; (5) the intention-to-treat check (:1072) cannot be substituted because all five dropped IDs are multi-copy (2, 2, 4, 4, 4 records) and are absent from the canonical per-pose table, so the 6.4 Å and 150-pose figures come from an unregistered source; (6) the cluster-analysis reach statistics (:1392, Fig r6) need a decision on what a "crystal cluster" is when a complex has several copies. Wording must change at :276, :662, :664, :1179, :1385 and :1397, and the regime-change disclosure (143/308, 138/303, median 36.0 Å, 25 Å cube excluded the copies, whole-protein box contains them) belongs at :664 with a pointer at :167/:1201. Five figures in this file are affected (image8, image11, image44-47) and one caption (:195) makes a depth-22 claim that will not survive unchanged.

decisions.question: How should contact and PLIF recovery (per_pose_metrics contact_recovery/plif_recovery; appendix :543, :549, :551, :1405, :1413, Figs r9 and main Fig 7) be referenced under nearest-copy, given that 139 of 143 alternate copies sit in the same pocket on another chain?
options: Build one PandaMap native fingerprint per record of <ID>_ligands.sdf and score each pose against the copy it is nearest to (consistent with the plan, large)
Keep contact recovery against the single reference and disclose the inconsistency (cheap, leaves poses on alternate copies scoring 0 matched)
Remap the reference fingerprint's chain identifier to the alternate copy's chain for the 139 same-pocket copies and profile only the four exceptions (7A9E_R4W, 7TUO_KL9, 7VKZ_NOJ, 7Z1Q_NIO) by hand
decisions.recommendation: Option 1, since the plan says every crystal-referenced metric follows the nearest copy and the interaction analysis is where a pose on an alternate copy is most distorted (all contacts spurious, all native contacts missed); option 3 is a validated shortcut only if the chain-remapped keys reproduce the profiled copy on a sample.

decisions.question: Which copy supplies the best-fit (Kabsch) RMSD that gates the 1 Å form endpoint and the top-15 triple gate that SELECTS variants (appendix :182, :230, :267, :1319-1336, :1375)?
options: Kabsch to the copy selected by in-place RMSD (one copy per pose, keeps r = form^2/in-place^2 coherent)
Minimum Kabsch over all copies independently of the in-place choice
Keep Kabsch to the single reference (conformer difference between copies is small)
decisions.recommendation: Option 1; the probe must be extended to emit it, and the triple-gate selection must be re-run before any table is rewritten because it decides which variants the tables print.

decisions.question: Is the metal-adjacent stratum (:165, 'within 5 Å of a crystal-ligand heavy atom', 78 of 303) re-evaluated per copy?
options: Keep the reference-copy definition and disclose
Define adjacency as a metal within 5 Å of any deposited copy
Define adjacency per pose against the copy it is scored on (not a complex-level label)
decisions.recommendation: Option 1 with a check that membership agrees on the 138 multi-copy complexes; the stratum source is not in the harness and must be located and registered first.

decisions.question: Does the conformer-generation difficulty descriptor (:754, :765, :782; median 1.56 Å, 65% within 2 Å; image40/image42) follow the nearest copy?
options: Keep on the single reference instance and say it is a start-conformer property, not a docking endpoint
Take the minimum Kabsch over copies and regenerate image40 and image42
decisions.recommendation: Option 1; it is not a docked-pose metric and the copies differ only conformationally.

decisions.question: What is a 'crystal cluster' in the pose-cluster analysis (:1392, :1397, Fig r5/r6) when a complex has several copies?
options: A pose cluster whose centroid lies within 4 Å of any deposited copy counts as a crystal cluster (several per complex allowed)
Only the cluster nearest the reference copy counts (current)
Report reach as 'any copy reached' but keep the per-complex crystal cluster unique by choosing the copy with most poses
decisions.recommendation: Option 1 for reach and the oracle ceiling (consistent with 98.0 -> 99.7%); the precision-at-one and consensus statistics then need their definitions restated because a tool can be right on two copies at once.

decisions.question: The confirmatory cell at :230 (+65.6 complexes per hour, 95% interval +32.1 to +137.2) was fixed in advance under the single-instance convention. Keep it on that convention or re-declare it?
options: Keep the confirmatory reading on the single-instance column and print the nearest-copy value beside it as descriptive
Re-declare the cell on the nearest-copy endpoint and say the switch post-dates the pre-specification
decisions.recommendation: Option 1; changing a pre-specified confirmatory cell after seeing the data is exactly what the paragraph says it avoids.

decisions.question: The intention-to-treat check at :1072 cannot be substituted because all five dropped complexes are multi-copy and absent from the canonical per-pose table. How is it re-established?
options: Re-score the 150 AutoDock poses of the five against <ID>_ligands.sdf with the probe engine and register the check as a harness stage
Drop the check and state that the exclusion sensitivity was not repeated under the new convention
decisions.recommendation: Option 1; the check is cheap and the five are exactly the kind of complex where the convention could flip a verdict.
